source_document.body:
2026 Paris Motor Show • The Volkswagen Group's Affordable BEV Quartet Has Almost Reached 150,000 Orders
The Volkswagen Group's Affordable BEV Quartet Has Almost Reached 150,000 Orders
27 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Is 150,000 a big number? If we're talking about clocking 150,000 orders for a quartet of entry-level electric vehicles before (supposedly) delivering a single one, it certainly sounds big. The Volkswagen ID. Polo, ID. Cross, Cupra Raval, and Skoda Epiq celebrated this near-milestone together at the Paris Motor Show, nearly a year after the Electric Urban Car Family was previewed at IAA Mobility in Munich.
The Electric Urban Car Family project has a straightforward origin story: develop a front-biased EV platform that maximizes interior space in the B segment, then develop four distinct and relatively affordable models across three brands on it. Said models slot below the compacts the Volkswagen Group builds on the rear-biased MEB platform, including the ID.4-turned-ID. Tiguan crossover.
To minimize development costs, all four models share their drivetrains and batteries. With these battery-electric vehicles, the Volkswagen Group is targeting one of the fastest-growing segments in Europe, a segment with prices regular people can actually reach. More than 80 percent of the components are shared, meaning that Volkswagen, Cupra, and Skoda did little more than stylistic work to differentiate these models.
Assembly work, however, splits by body style. Both the ID. Polo and Raval are considered superminis, with production being handled by the Martorell plant in Spain. Their crossover equivalents, namely the ID. Cross and the Epiq, hail from the Pamplona facility in Spain. Of course, the Volkswagen Group invested a lot of money into SEAT and the SEAT-born Cupra division to make this Spanish production complex possible.
The 2026 Paris Motor Show wasn't just a photo op, though. This edition was used by Skoda to reveal the Sportline trim leve l, complete with matrix LED headlights and 19-inch wheels. The Epiq Sportline can be had in 40 and 55 flavors, and in the UK, it slots above the Edition 55.
Photo: Volkswagen All in all, the Wolfsburg-based colossus wouldn't have reached almost 150,000 orders for B-segment electric vehicles that (supposedly) haven't even started deliveries without serious demand for attractively priced subcompacts. Beyond the attractive prices, their democratized technologies and versatility also helped drive consumer demand in the Old Continent.
That's 150,00 orders from buyers who are committing to vehicles they haven't driven, and that kind of commercial success is built on three pillars: asking price, the product's competitive strengths, and brand trust. In this particular segment, where margins are pretty slim and every platform decision is ruthless from a financial standpoint, this kind of order bank should be viewed as a verdict the market handed down before the launch.
It's not all smooth sailing, though. Both Martorell-built hatchbacks have been hit with their first recalls, with Germany's KBA explaining that 1,109 units of the ID. Polo may be hindered by a B-pillar seatbelt anchorage flaw . Under a different campaign, the Cupra brand is recalling a total of 10,151 Terramar and Raval vehicles produced through September 3, 2026, as opposed to September 2, 2026, for the suspect ID. Polo hatchbacks.
The Ravals and Terramars are suspected of insufficiently fastened lower seatbelt anchors . Relatively small populations, for sure, but said recalls demonstrate that new products come with new challenges for the people employed to assemble them. Fortunately for everyone, both fixes are reassuringly simple.
